note: Second predicate for #3092, measuring the CAPABILITY rather than the diagnostic. The request is that the SPIR-V workgroup size be driveable by a specialization constant; Vulkan accepts exactly two spellings for that, and this asserts neither is present: the `LocalSizeId` execution mode naming the spec constant (SPIR-V 1.2+, Vulkan 1.3 / VK_KHR_maintenance4), or a `BuiltIn WorkgroupSize`-decorated OpSpecConstantComposite (the form glslc emits, quoted by @shangjiaxuan on the issue). It exists because match.json is anchored on one particular diagnostic: if some release ACCEPTED the attribute and silently folded the spec constant to its initialiser, match.json would score no-repro and read as a fix, while this predicate would still match. That shape did not occur -- all 19 probeable releases error -- so this predicate confirms rather than carries the verdict. THIS IS AN ABSENCE-ONLY PREDICATE and SKILL.md is explicit that such a predicate is satisfied for free by a compile that never started; `run` warns about exactly that on every probe of repro.hlsl. It is not evidence on its own, only alongside the primary probes and its controls. CONTROLS, both captured: (1) variant-execmodeid.hlsl at -fspv-target-env=vulkan1.3 reaches LocalSizeId through the inline-SPIR-V escape hatch `vk::ext_execution_mode_id(38, TGSIZE_X, 1u, 1u)`, and this predicate correctly does not match it (--expect no-match) -- that is what shows the predicate is falsifiable rather than vacuously true; (2) control-specconst-literal.hlsl compiles successfully and this predicate DOES match it (--expect match), which shows the match on repro.hlsl is not merely riding on the compile having failed. TRAP, measured here and recorded in method-notes.md: the same variant at the DEFAULT target environment is rejected, and DXC's own message quotes the offending instruction back -- `2nd operand of ExecutionModeId: operand LocalSizeId(38) requires SPIR-V version 1.2 or later` followed by the instruction itself. A text-absence predicate cannot tell that apart from a successful emission, so that capture scores no-match even though nothing usable was emitted. Anchoring the regex on `OpExecutionModeId ... LocalSizeId` would not help: the validator echoes the whole instruction verbatim.
